quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if there is no traffic crossing.
Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the intersection is dangerous. Treat it exactly like a stop sign.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would get in the way of other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car ahead is broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would get in the way of other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you do it safely and do not block other traffic.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may move in the direction the arrow points if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers must always stop completely before moving in the direction the arrow points.
Drivers in that lane must move in the direction the arrow points while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must move in the direction the arrow points while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells drivers in that lane they must move in that direction. Always follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: When you want to turn right, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as you can. Do not cross other lanes to make any turn.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lane and there is a cyclist ahead going the same way. How should you safely pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. It is the cyclist's job to move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk so the cyclist knows you are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet between your mirror and the cyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or with a group of cyclists. Do not honk suddenly as it can scare them.

questions.question: When passing a car that just parked on the side of the road, what should you assume?

options.text: The driver will open the car door as you pass.
Speed up.
Brake hard.
The driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will open the car door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, assume the driver will open the door as you approach. Be extra careful around parked vehicles.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a wide intersection and cannot see all the lanes because of traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up as soon as the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all the lanes before turning.
Wait for another driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane of traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes are clear and you can turn safely.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Keep the same
Change
Lower

questions.correctAnswerText: Lower
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning so you can control your car, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You will be found more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You will be found more easily.
questions.explanation: If you are stuck in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: You are late for work. Before backing into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Check for children and objects around your car.
Rev your engine to scare animals away.
Check for traffic before you get in the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for children and objects around your car.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see well. Be very careful when backing in neighborhoods where children often play behind or between parked cars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
The road ahead curves to the left, then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for road hazards. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid brake damage or crashes.

questions.question: When an oncoming car is to your left and a bicyclist is to your right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Split the difference.
Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Do not try to pass the bike while the car is coming toward you. Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" can result from:

options.text: Staring at the road for long periods of time.
Frequent rest stops.
Too much sleep the night before.
Short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for too long and stop looking around. You may zone out and crash into traffic ahead of you. Keep scanning left, right, and behind.

questions.question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the same speed and proceed.
Stop, check all directions, and proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to traffic coming from the right. Always be ready to stop. Release the gas, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules for that area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from crossing guards, signs, and police in school zones. Drive slowly and carefully in these areas.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
The reduced speed zone is starting.
You may see more pedestrians.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times posted. When you see an "End school zone" sign, the reduced speed area has ended.

questions.question: Bicyclists must not:

options.text: Carry passengers unless the bike is designed for it.
Ride on sidewalks anywhere.
Ride at night.
Ride in the road in a business district.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carry passengers unless the bike is designed for it.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists cannot ride on sidewalks in business districts, but can in other areas at 10 mph or slower while yielding to pedestrians. Bicyclists can ride at night with lights and reflectors. Never carry passengers on a bike unless it is made for that.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are turning.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
Keep the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so the driver can see you.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
You can pass from the lane with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: How far back should you follow the car ahead of you?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
100 feet.
75 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second gap between your car and the car ahead. This helps you avoid rear-end collisions.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that cars are backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull over to the right side and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: If you are driving much slower than other traffic on a two-lane road, pull off the road to let cars pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull off the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull over to the side of the road.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is coming toward you on a two-lane street. What should you do?

options.text: Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to the right as far as possible, and stop.
Ignore it because it is going the opposite direction.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right as far as possible, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you see or hear an emergency vehicle, slow down and move as far to the right as you can, then stop. This applies even if the vehicle is coming from the opposite direction. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must you account for?

options.text: Trucks need more distance to stop.
Trucks need less distance to stop.
Trucks make less noise.
Trucks drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more stopping distance than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where your view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: Is night driving more or less dangerous than day driving?

options.text: Less dangerous.
About the same.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because it is harder to see, headlight glare can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Obey all traffic signals.
Watch for pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways at train tracks, obey all traffic signals, and watch for pedestrians and bicyclists sharing the road.

questions.question: How should you merge into traffic on a crowded freeway?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to match the freeway speed.
Let freeway traffic go first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure it is safe. Let traffic already on the freeway go first.
